To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the inhomogeneous mixing of gas clouds in a stochastic scenario of star formation and supernova explosions can explain the observed abundance patterns of heavy elements in the Galactic halo.
inhomogeneous chemical enrichment of the halo can explain the observed abundance of r-process elements in metal-poor halo field stars.

(1) the stochastic model is a powerful tool to investigate the inhomogeneous and delayed enrichment of the Galactic halo; (2) the chemical evolution of the halo depends on the supernova progenitor mass range and on the mass spectrum of interstellar gas fragments, with a significant impact on the predicted abundance of r-process elements in halo stars.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the chemical evolution of the Galaxy and, in particular, of the Galactic halo, with a focus on the inhomogeneous evolution of the interstellar medium, and the enrichment of the interstellar and halo gas by supernova nucleosynthesis.

the following issues: (a) the chemical evolution of the halo gas in a stochastic scenario; (b) the production of r-process elements in supernova explosions and its consequences on the chemical evolution of metal-poor stars; and (c) the chemical evolution in the presence of infalling gas.
the chemical and dynamical evolution of galaxies, in particular the Milky Way.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the inhomogeneous model is able to account for most of the features observed in the abundance of r-process elements, but it is not able to reproduce the abundance distribution in the most metal-poor stars, which are characterized by very large [Ba/Eu] and very low [Sr/Eu] ratios.

the inhomogeneous evolution of the Galactic disk and halo is a very promising approach to explain the abundance patterns of metal-poor stars in the Galaxy, and that the stochastic nature of the star formation process is crucial in order to understand the observed abundance patterns.

our inhomogeneous model, which takes into account the stochastic nature of the star formation history and the delayed mixing into the interstellar gas, is capable of explaining the observed age-metallicity relation and the G-dwarfs distribution in the halo.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a model that can reproduce the age-metallicity and G-dwarf distributions of the Galactic halo, as well as the abundance of elements produced by r-process nucleosythesis, in agreement with the observed abundances of metal-poor stars.
our model is consistent with the observational data for the abundance of r-process elements in the Galactic halo.

we have shown that a model based on the fragmentation and coagulation of interstellar clouds is able to reproduce many observed properties of the Galactic halo, including the G-dwarf problem and the inhomogeneous distribution of heavy elements.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the inhomogeneity of star formation in the early Galactic halo, combined with the delayed mixing of the ejecta of supernova explosions, can explain the observed chemical properties of metal-poor stars in the halo.

the chemical enrichment of the Galactic halo can be explained by the combined action of supernovae of different masses, and that the observed abundance pattern of r-process elements can be reproduced by our model if we assume that the supernova progenitors have masses in the range from 12 to 40 Msolar.

the inhomogeneous nature of the chemical evolution of the halo is a key ingredient for the production of r-process elements in a realistic way, as the mixing of the intergalactic gas is the only mechanism able to reproduce the observed abundance of Eu in halo stars.
